newsitem.title: USA: Harris County, Texas, mulls $250 mln issue in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Harris County, Texas, mulls $250 mln issue in Nov.

text.p: Harris County, Texas, is considering a roughly $250 million bond offering for sometime in November, Faye Christopher, the county's director of Financial Services, said Thursday.
Though still tentative, plans call for $80 million of refunding bonds and $165 million of new money, Christopher said.

Tuesday, Commissioners Court, Harris County's governing body, approved a restructuring of the county's debt. Christopher said she must now go back before the court next Tuesday with a bond order for the issue's authorization. The county currently has $2.7 billion of debt outstanding.
"After the restructuring is accomplished it would add an additional $650 million (approximately) of borrowing capacity," Christopher said.

As for the $165 million new money portion, $80 million will go toward road improvement, and marks the last of the county's voter-approved road bond money. The remaining $85 million will go for construction of a 20-floor criminal court building project called the Criminal Justice Center.
